title: Why an SEC Director Calls a WSJ Ad on Tokenized Stocks ‘Misleading’
description: SEC trading director Jamie Selway disputed two claims in an October Wall Street Journal advertisement opposing tokenized stocks, while Securitize's Brett Redfearn discussed issuer objections and market competition.
why_it_matters: The disagreement highlights how the design of tokenized share trading, investor rights and regulatory exemptions could influence issuer participation. Selway's remarks are an interpretation of the proposed framework, not a new SEC rule or approval of any trading venue.
keyTakeaways: SEC trading director Jamie Selway challenged an October newspaper advertisement's characterization of tokenized-stock trading as unregulated.
Selway said the tokenized-share structure under discussion should preserve underlying shareholder rights rather than create synthetic claims.
Securitize president Brett Redfearn described competitive tensions and said his firm published a response to the advertisement.
body:
In an Unchained interview excerpt published on November 18, Jamie Selway, director of the US Securities and Exchange Commission's Division of Trading and Markets, challenged an advertisement warning public-company executives about tokenized shares. The advertisement appeared in the Wall Street Journal in late October and was attributed in the interview to the Common Sense Leadership Fund.

Selway said the advertisement was misleading in two respects. First, he disputed the suggestion that the relevant tokenized-share trading arrangements were entirely unregulated, pointing to requirements associated with exempt entities, including permissioned wallets, public notice and SEC examinations. Second, he rejected the implication that a token necessarily separates holders from the rights attached to the underlying security. His comments described the framework under discussion; they did not announce a new regulation.

Brett Redfearn, president of Securitize, said his company had run a responding advertisement and argued that incumbent intermediaries may view alternative trading structures as competitive threats. The conversation also discussed issuer objections to the OKX ICE tokenized-stock initiative. Those objections and the October advertisement provide context for the November interview, rather than evidence of a newly launched trading product.

sources.name: Unchained interview transcript via Yahoo Finance

facts.claim: The Unchained interview featured SEC trading director Jamie Selway and Securitize president Brett Redfearn discussing tokenized shares.
The advertisement discussed in the interview ran in the Wall Street Journal in late October.
Selway rejected the characterization of the tokenized share arrangements as completely unregulated and mentioned permissioned wallets.
Selway said the arrangement was intended to represent the rights and privileges of security holders on tokens.
Redfearn said Securitize had run a separate newspaper advertisement in response to the earlier advertisement.
The interview discussed issuer objections to tokenized stock trading on the OKX ICE venue.
